How life has changed in Teignbridge: Census 2021


Teignbridge's population increased by around 10,600 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.


Select an alternative area


19 January 2023


The population passed 130,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Teignbridge increased by 8.5%, from around 124,200 in 2011 to around 134,800 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the South West (7.8%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Teignbridge was home to around 1.4 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 1.3 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 25% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

An older Teignbridge

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Teignbridge increased by two years, from 47 to 49 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the South West as a whole in 2021 (44 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 4,400 (an increase of 30.1%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 2,600 (10.5% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 2.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Teignbridge stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased in Teignbridge, but fell across England.

In Teignbridge, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 8.9% in 2011 to 9.5% in 2021, while across England it fell from 17.7% to 17.1%. During the same period, the regional percentage remained at 13.3%.

Private renting in Teignbridge increased from 15.5% to 17.9%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 73.5% to 71.3%.

Disability in Teignbridge

The age-standardised proportion of non-disabled residents fell here, but rose across England.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In Teignbridge, the proportion of non-disabled residents fell from 81.8% in 2011 to 81.4% in 2021, while across England it rose from 80.7% to 82.3%. During the same period, the regional proportion increased from 81.9% to 82.2%.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Teignbridge fell from 8.0% to 7.2%, while the percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little increased from 10.2% to 11.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

Religion in Teignbridge

In 2021, 44.8% of Teignbridge residents reported having "No religion", up from 28.1% in 2011. The rise of 16.7 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Teignbridge. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South West, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 29.3% to 44.1%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 47.2% of people in Teignbridge described themselves as Christian (down from 62.2%), while 6.4% did not state their religion (down from 8.4% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Teignbridge residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 124,100 Teignbridge residents said they were born in England. This represented 92.1% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 114,600 in 2011, which at the time represented 92.3% of Teignbridge's population.

Wales was the next most represented, with around 1,900 Teignbridge residents reporting this country of birth (1.4%). This figure was down from around 2,000 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.6% of the population of Teignbridge.

The number of Teignbridge residents born in Scotland remained close to 1,500 between the last two census (from 1.2% of the local population in 2011 to 1.1% in 2021)

National identity in Teignbridge

In 2021, 2.8% of Teignbridge residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.1% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.2% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.4% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Teignbridge that identified as "British only" increased from 15.3% to 57.1%.

This area had the region’s second lowest percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. Across the region, only Torridge, with 2.1%, had a lower percentage.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Teignbridge increased by 0.7 percentage points

Unpaid care in Teignbridge

In 2021, 5.1% of Teignbridge residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.9% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.8%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.4% in 2011. The proportion of Teignbridge residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.6% to 2.8%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Teignbridge (2.8 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South West (2.8 percentage points, from 7.5% to 4.7%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

Health in Teignbridge

In 2021, 49.1% of Teignbridge residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 47.6% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.4% to 33.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Teignbridge residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.0% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" remained 3.7%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Family in Teignbridge

Of Teignbridge households, 19.1% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 20.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in six households (16.4%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 17.9% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 5.8% to 6.0%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Teignbridge (1.5 percentage points) than across the South West (1.2 percentage points, from 19.7% to 18.5%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Teignbridge residents aged 16 years and over, 29.4% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 26.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (49.1%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 52.0% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Teignbridge that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 10.9% to 11.6%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Teignbridge (3.3 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South West (3.5 percentage points, from 31.1% to 34.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

Change in employment

Of Teignbridge residents aged 16 years and over, 53.7% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 55.5% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.8%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.4% in 2011. The percentage of retired Teignbridge residents increased from 29.2% to 30.6%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed in Teignbridge (1.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South West (1.6 percentage points, from 56.9% to 55.3%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

Change in work hours

In 2021, 11.7% of Teignbridge residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 11.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in nine people (11.2%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 13.8% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 52.7% to 54.1%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week in Teignbridge (0.4 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South West (0.5 percentage points, from 10.8% to 11.3%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

Ethnic groups in Teignbridge

In 2021, 1.2% of Teignbridge residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 0.7% in 2011. The 0.4 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South West, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 1.4% to 2.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 97.7% of people in Teignbridge identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 98.3% in 2011), while 0.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (also 0.7% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.1% in 2011 to 0.3% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

About the data

Census data are adjusted to reflect estimated non-response so that the published results relate to the entire usually resident population as it was on Census Day (21 March 2021).

Those respondents who were on furlough because of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic were asked to classify themselves as "temporarily away from work" to ensure they remained in the economically active population.

Students are counted as usually resident at their term-time address even if they were not physically present there on Census Day.

The questions relating to disability differed slightly between 2011 and 2021 to ensure that data were more closely aligned with the definition of disability in the Equality Act (2010). There was also a change to question wording for unpaid care, for more information read the health, disability and unpaid care quality information.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout the health, disability and unpaid care sections. They allow for fairer comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure. The 2013 European Standard Population is used to standardise proportions.

Percentages and percentage point changes have been individually rounded to one decimal place. This means they may not sum exactly.

About these articles

There is an article like this for every local authority district in England and Wales. The articles have been written and semi-automated by our data journalists and are a new publishing format for the Office for National Statistics.

Topics are chosen and ordered automatically based on how relevant they are for each area, however all data are checked before publishing.

We have not included topics that were new for Census 2021 or where there is no comparability with the 2011 Census. Read about how we developed and tested the questions for Census 2021.

These articles were first published on 8 December 2022 covering topics such as demography, country of birth, ethnic groups, religion, national identity and economic activity status. They were updated on 19 January 2023 following the release of more data from Census 2021 and now include housing tenure, general health, disability and unpaid care.
